instrument: Model Building Bye-Laws 2016 (MBBL), MoHUA; rainwater harvesting chapter
applicability_threshold: all buildings having a plot size of 100 sq.m or more (RWH proposal required with building plan)
penalty_or_incentive: NR (states decide)
enforcing_agency: State governments / Urban Local Bodies / Urban Development Authorities
reported_compliance: 33 States/UTs have adopted the RWH provisions (Lok Sabha reply 05.03.2020; also PIB 24.03.2020); 'barring Sikkim, Lakshadweep and Mizoram' all States/UTs adopted (Lok Sabha Q1241, 09.02.2023)
quote: Lok Sabha USQ 2478 (05.03.2020): 'The provisions of this chapter are applicable to all the buildings.' ... 33 States/UTs have adopted the rainwater harvesting provisions. Lok Sabha USQ 1241 (09.02.2023): 'all buildings having a plot size of 100 sq.m or, more' must include a rainwater harvesting proposal; 'barring Sikkim, Lakshadweep and Mizoram' all States/UTs have adopted the MBBL-2016 provisions. Yahoo/PTI: '33 States/ Union Territories have adopted the rainwater harvesting feature under Model Building Bye Laws, 2016.'

instrument: Tamil Nadu Municipal Laws (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2003 (TN Ordinance No. 4 of 2003) inserting s.255-A Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act etc.
applicability_threshold: every owner or occupier of a building (all buildings; Govt buildings too)
penalty_or_incentive: water supply connection disconnected until structure provided; Commissioner may build and recover cost as property tax; new buildings not given water/sewer connection without RWH (CSE)
enforcing_agency: Municipal Corporations / Municipalities (Commissioner / Executive Authority); CMWSSB
reported_compliance: Chennai 2019: GCC inspected ~2.72 lakh houses since Aug 2019, ~1.62 lakh had RWH (approx 60%), 9,000 notices issued; CMWSSB claims 8.9 lakh structures; Rain Centre 2015 audit of 1,100 samples found govt buildings worst violators
quote: Ordinance: 'TAMIL NADU ORDINANCE No.4 OF 2003' ... 'every owner or occupier of a building shall provide rain water harvesting structure in the building' ... water supply connection 'shall be disconnected' until the structure is provided. TNM 2 Sep 2019: 'The Greater Chennai Corporation has sent notices to 9,000 houses without rainwater harvesting structures.' 'conducted inspections in around 2.72 lakh houses, since August.' 'Around 1.62 lakh houses that were inspected had rainwater harvesting structures in place.' TNM 20 Jun 2019: CMWSSB data shows 'over 8.9 lakh rainwater harvesting structures in various buildings across the city'; Rain Centre 2015 audit: government buildings were 'the worst violators of the rainwater harvesting rule'.

instrument: Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage (Amendment) Act, 2011 (Karnataka Act No. 05 of 2011) substituting s.72A (bill introduced 2009); penalty regulations 2015; BWSS (Amendment) Bill 2021 extends to 30x40 sites
applicability_threshold: existing buildings on sital area >= 2400 sq ft (60x40 ft site); new buildings on sital area >= 1200 sq ft (30x40 ft); 2021 Bill: sital area 2,325-10,763.9 sq ft RWH; >=10,763.9 sq ft dual piping + RWH
penalty_or_incentive: residential: 25% of water bill first 3 months then 50%; non-residential: 50% then 100% (Citizen Matters 2023); Rs 1.95-2 crore/month collected
enforcing_agency: Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB)
reported_compliance: Dec 2023: ~1.9 lakh of 10.8 lakh properties with water connections (~18%) have RWH; 39,703 properties paying monthly penalty; Mar 2024 (The Hindu): 1,96,591 residential buildings implemented, 39,213 have not
quote: Act: 'Every owner or occupier of a building having sital area of not less than 2400 square feet' 'or every owner who propose to construct a building on a sital area of not less than 1200 square feet' 'shall provide rain water harvesting structure for storage for use or for ground water recharge'. Citizen Matters 7 Dec 2023: 'The BWSSB Amendment Act, 2011, made RWH mandatory for all properties on plots measuring 60X40 sq ft and above.' ... fine is 25% of the water bill for the first three months then 50% (residential); 50% then 100% (non-residential); about 1.9 lakh of 10.8 lakh properties (nearly 18%); 39,703 properties paying monthly penalties, Rs 1.95 crore in October; BWSSB 'not clear how many properties exactly are supposed to implement RWH'. The Hindu 21 Mar 2024: '1,96,591 residential buildings have implemented RWH systems'; '39,213 buildings have not'; 'the Board has been collecting Rs 1.98 crore - Rs 2 crore as penalty for nonimplementation of RWH' each month since July 2016.

instrument: Government orders for Government buildings; statewide urban mandate 'contemplated' (2011); 20% tax rebate (CSE)
applicability_threshold: Government buildings; amendment of bye-laws in cities >20 lakh population under action (CSE); statewide new buildings contemplated 2011
penalty_or_incentive: 20% rebate on tax payment for 5 years (CSE)
reported_compliance: NR
quote: CSE: Karnataka 'has issued orders for implementation of roof top rainwater harvesting in all Government buildings'; 'Action to amend building byelaws in major cities having population of more than 20 lakh'; '20% rebate on tax payment for 5 years duration'. Deccan Herald 14 Jan 2011: government is 'contemplating making rainwater harvesting structures mandatory in newly-constructed buildings in all urban pockets across the state'.

instrument: Building Bye-laws 1983 modified by MoUD Gazette Notification 28.07.2001 (plots >=100 sq m); CGWA directive; DJB resolution No. 829; Unified Building Bye-Laws 2016
year_enforced: 2001 (plan sanction); DJB penalty enforced after deadlines extended to 2021/2022
applicability_threshold: all buildings with plot area >= 100 sq m (2001 notification; DJB resolution 829); DJB compulsory for plots >= 500 sq m; UBBL 2016 features mandatory for new constructions above 105 sq m (DUAC)
penalty_or_incentive: building plans not sanctioned without RWH; DJB 10% rebate on water bill for plots >= 100 sq m with functional RWH; penalty 1.5 times water bill / '50% of the monthly bill amount' for non-compliance; proposed environmental compensation Rs 50,000 to Rs 5 lakh (2023 proposal); NGT Rs 5 lakh per educational institution (OA 217/2016)
enforcing_agency: DJB (rebate/penalty); DDA/MCD (plan sanction, completion certificate); DPCC; NGT monitoring

quote: DPCC report (NGT, Feb 2024): 'modifications / additions to the Building by laws, 1983, made vide Gazette Notification dated 28.07.2001' ... 'all the buildings having plot area greater that or equal to 100 sq. mtr regarding rain water harvesting'; DJB: 'shall attract a penalty of inflated 50% of the monthly bill amount'; NGT O.A. 217/2016: 'Rs. 5 Lakh per institution required to be paid by educational institutions'. jurisdiction: Mumbai / Maharashtra (Greater Mumbai DCR; all towns non-gaothan)
instrument: Govt of Maharashtra UDD Notification No. TPB-4307/396/CR-124/2007/UD-11 dated 6 June 2007 modifying Development Control Regulations for Greater Mumbai 1991; BMC mandatory for new buildings since 2002 (Citizen Matters); Aug 2026 GR: old buildings seeking new water/drainage connections must have RWH
applicability_threshold: plots having area not less than 300 sq m in non-gaothan areas of all towns (2007); earlier 1,000 sq m (CSE)
penalty_or_incentive: no building permission unless provision for RWH; levy not exceeding Rs 1000 per annum per 100 sq m built-up area for failure to provide/maintain; completion/occupation certificate only after RWH (CSE)
enforcing_agency: Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (BMC) Hydraulic Engineer dept; Planning Authority
reported_compliance: approx. 3,000 societies of an estimated 20,000 had RWH 2007-2021 (Citizen Matters Jul 2024)
quote: MCGM PDF: Notification 'No. TPB-4307/396/CR-124/2007/UD-11' dated 6th June 2007; 'plots having area not less than 300 sq.mt. in non gaothan areas of all towns'; 'no building permssion be granted unless provision is made for Rain Water Harvesting Scheme'; Authority 'may impose a levy of not exceeding Rs.1000/- per annum for every 100 sq.mt. of built up area'. Citizen Matters 17 Jul 2024: 'the BMC has made rainwater harvesting mandatory for new buildings since 2002'; 'Approximately only 3000 societies of the total' (of an estimated 20,000) had RWH 2007-2021; 'most societies neglect it, once OC is received'; 'the rebate never reflected in their society bills'. CSE: 'Completion certificate to buildings is granted only after installation of RWH structure(s)'. ThePrint 10 Aug 2026: 'Old buildings in Maharashtra seeking new water or drainage connections' must have 'provisions for rainwater harvesting and bio-sludge management systems'.

instrument: AP Govt order (2000) for all municipal corporations/urban areas (IWP); APWALTA 2002; HMWSSB directive dated 14 Dec 2024 for 17,000 consumers

South First 22 Dec 2024: 'The notices were based on data collected by 18 NGOs, which had surveyed 39,000 properties.'; 'at least 17,000 water consumers within the Greater Hyderabad area'; 'those failing to meet the deadline would face double charges for HMWSSB water tankers.' Realty Today 19 Dec 2024: 'identified 42,000 buildings in need of rainwater harvesting systems'; '17,000 properties remain non-compliant'; 'this requirement was modified to 300 square meters or above'.

instrument: Rajasthan state mandate (PHED certification); Jaipur/Rajasthan Building Bye-Laws 2020 Regulation 21.7 (rule 10.11.1); JDA enforcement 2011
